topic.subject: social
topic.title: The Delhi Sultans
topic.scope: Slave, Khalji and Tughluq dynasties, iqta system, Alauddin Khalji's reforms, Muhammad bin Tughluq's experiments, Raziya

concepts.name: Nature of Dynastic Rule and Sultans

misconceptions.statement: The Delhi Sultans were all kings who inherited the throne from their fathers.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the Delhi Sultanate with the later Mughal Empire where hereditary succession was the norm.
misconceptions.fix: The Delhi Sultanate was not strictly hereditary; many Sultans, especially in the Slave dynasty, were military commanders or slaves who rose to power through merit and force.

probe.question: How did Raziya Sultan become the ruler of Delhi?
probe.wrong_answer: She inherited the throne from her father because she was the eldest son.

misconceptions.statement: All Sultans were absolute monarchs who had total control over their entire kingdom.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks focus on the capital city, leading students to assume the Sultan's power was uniform across all territories.
misconceptions.fix: Sultans often struggled to control distant provinces, and their authority was frequently challenged by local chieftains and rebellious governors.

probe.question: Why did the Sultans have trouble controlling Bengal or South India?
probe.wrong_answer: They didn't have trouble; they had absolute power everywhere in India.

misconceptions.statement: The Iqta was a piece of land owned by the military commander forever.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the Iqta system with the later Zamindari system where land rights became hereditary.
misconceptions.fix: An Iqta was a temporary assignment of revenue collection rights, not ownership of the land, and the commander was frequently transferred.

probe.question: What happened to an iqtadar after a few years?
probe.wrong_answer: He stayed on his land and passed it down to his children.

misconceptions.statement: Muhammad bin Tughluq moved his capital to Daulatabad because he wanted to go on a vacation.
misconceptions.why: Students often attribute complex political or strategic decisions to simple personal whims or personality traits.
misconceptions.fix: The capital was moved to Daulatabad to better control the southern territories of the empire, which was a strategic administrative decision.

probe.question: Why did Muhammad bin Tughluq shift his capital?
probe.wrong_answer: He just liked the weather in the south and wanted to move his palace.

misconceptions.statement: Alauddin Khalji lowered prices just because he was a kind person who cared about the poor.
misconceptions.why: Students project modern democratic values of 'welfare' onto medieval rulers.
misconceptions.fix: Alauddin Khalji controlled prices to maintain a large standing army at low costs, not as a social welfare measure for the common people.

probe.question: Why did Alauddin Khalji keep the prices of grain low?
probe.wrong_answer: He wanted to make sure the poor people in Delhi could afford to eat.
